title: 3 משחקי קופסא שיעזרו להם לשאול ולתאר דברים

stage.need: Using more words and longer sentences, answering and asking questions, describing things. CDC lists 'Says sentences with four or more words' and 'Answers simple questions' among the 4 year milestones and 'Keeps a conversation going with more than three back-and-forth exchanges' among the 5 year milestones; KidsHealth names 'playing word games' and 'asking questions' as everyday ways to support vocabulary at 4 to 5. A guessing game and a naming game give a playful reason to ask, describe and name things aloud (an opportunity to practise, not a guarantee).
stage.age_caveat: Ages are approximate: milestones describe what most children (75 percent or more) do by an age, not a deadline. Some 4 year olds already hold a conversation and some 5 year olds are still building sentences; copy should say בערך / יש ילדים ש... Both games print an age at or below 4 (4+ and 2-6 on the boxes), so the stage's minimum age (4) is not below either game's official minimum.

dev_sources.title: Milestones by 4 Years
dev_sources.publisher: CDC, Learn the Signs. Act Early.
dev_sources.quote: Says sentences with four or more words / Answers simple questions like "What is a coat for?" or "What is a crayon for?" / Play simple games, such as Tic-Tac-Toe or matching games.
dev_sources.supports: 4 year language milestones (sentences of four or more words; answers simple questions about what things are for) plus the tip to play simple games and matching games. Read today in the in-app browser (plain curl gets 403); sentences joined with ' / ' in page order (milestone list, then the tips list). The page does not say board games build vocabulary; it lists games only as a general tip. Milestones are what 75 percent or more of children do by an age.

dev_sources.title: Milestones by 5 Years
dev_sources.publisher: CDC, Learn the Signs. Act Early.
dev_sources.quote: Keeps a conversation going with more than three back-and-forth exchanges / Ask your child what she is playing. Help her expand her answers by asking "Why?" and "How?" / Play games that help with memory and attention. For example, play card games, Tic Tac Toe, I Spy, or Hot and Cold.
dev_sources.supports: 5 year conversation milestone and the tips to ask 'Why?' and 'How?' while a child plays and to play card games. Read today in the in-app browser; sentences joined with ' / ' in page order. The tips are general parenting tips, not about these two products, and the page does not mention board games for vocabulary specifically.

dev_sources.title: Language Development in Your 4- to 5-Year-Old
dev_sources.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (medically reviewed by Mary L. Gavin, MD, May 2022)
dev_sources.quote: Reading books, singing, playing word games, asking questions, and talking to your kids will help increase vocabulary and improve their listening skills.
dev_sources.supports: Names 'playing word games' and 'asking questions' among everyday ways to support vocabulary at 4 to 5. A general parent explainer, not research on board games; its own wording is 'will help', so our copy must soften it to 'a chance to practise' (no claim that a game causes vocabulary growth).

popularity_signals.description: Displayed position 21 of 463 in the Toys R Us Israel board-games collection sorted by the store's own 'הנמכרים ביותר' option (a sales sort of undisclosed time window, not a published chart). Page 1 of 12 read on 2026-10-13 and products counted in page order (40 per page); the store shows in-stock items first within a page, so the position is exact to the page and approximate inside it. Position 21 of 463 is 4.5 percent, inside the top 10 percent (about 46), so it counts as a strong signal; it is one place outside the top 20.
Listed and in stock at several independent Israeli sellers: Toys R Us Israel, Center Toys, and the publisher's own shop (pages opened 2026-10-13).
Hebrew-language game made and published by Kodkod, a long-established Israeli games publisher (Kodkod logo and Hebrew text on the box; Kodkod product page).

products.popularity_reasoning: One strong signal (Toys R Us Israel sales sort, 21 of 463, inside the top 10 percent) plus two supporting signals from different groups (three Israeli sellers; established Israeli publisher). The sort is a store sales ranking of undisclosed window, not a published chart.
products.developmental_relevance: Each child wears a headband with a picture card they cannot see and asks questions to find out what it is; Kodkod: 'אין צורך במיומנות הקריאה והכתיבה' and 'המפתח את כושר הביטוי'. Every turn is a chance to practise asking a question in a full sentence and to answer with a word or a short sentence, which sits next to CDC's 4 to 5 year language milestones (sentences, answering questions, conversation).
products.parent_tip_source: Our suggestion, from Kodkod's rules (young children can play with one petal, one category): start with one category such as animals and ask the child to say the whole question ('האם אני חיה?') instead of pointing; CDC tip: ask 'Why?' and 'How?' to help a child expand answers.

Page 5 of 12 read on 2026-10-13 and products counted in page order (40 per page); the store shows in-stock items first within a page, so the position is exact to the page and approximate inside it. products.popularity_reasoning: No strong signal (167 of 463 is outside the top 10 percent). Three supporting signals from three groups: Toys R Us sales sort, four Israeli sellers, established Israeli publisher. popular_in_israel through the two-signal route, but the weaker of the two games.
products.developmental_relevance: Kodkod's own text says the 12-pair 'introduction' way to play has children get to know the words for the pictures and so develop conversation ('עורכים היכרות עם המילים השונות וכך מפתחים שיחה'); in the memory way to play each turn turns over two photo cards, so there is a reason to name each picture aloud. CDC's 4 year tip lists 'matching games', and the 5 year tip lists games for memory and attention. Naming pictures aloud is an opportunity to practise vocabulary (the pairs memory itself is not a language task).
products.parent_tip_source: Our suggestion, from Kodkod's first way to play (stack the 12 pairs and guess which card comes up): say the name of every picture out loud together, and ask 'מה עושים עם זה?' (CDC 4 year milestone: answers what a thing is for).

image.rights_note: Kodkod's own packshot of the Hebrew box (itempics image on the product page; the box shows '2-6'). No press kit or media licence seen. 779 px is just under the preferred 800; Toys R Us hosts a similar-size copy so no larger version was found.

products.limitations: Popularity rests on supporting signals only (the store ranking is a sales sort of unknown window, position approximate inside a page). Bug lists it but out of stock. Age: box 2-6, Kodkod groups 2-3/4-5/6-8, Center Toys 2+, Toys R Us spec field says 2-4 (looks like a template value, and wrongly suggests it tops out at 4). Pairs memory is a memory game first: its link to vocabulary rests on Kodkod's own wording about naming the words and on the parent adding talk. Kodkod is on the 'prefer other makers' warning list and both games are Kodkod. The two games are different types (question guessing vs pairs matching).

image.depicts: A small boy in a grey shirt with an orange sleeve sits on a bed in a softly lit room with string lights, holding a glowing microphone, musical notes floating around him as he looks up and sings: the idea of the line, finding a magic microphone and singing out loud. No readable lettering on the cover (a tiny shirt pocket mark only).

lumebook.connection: Second to last of 3 suggestions (2 games and the LumeBook book), in Yarin's format: ספר של LumeBook / סיפור מותאם אישית עם תמונה של הילדים שלכם שבו... Catalogue book 45 (ages 3 to 6, a shy child who finds a magic microphone and learns to sing in front of others) is the closest catalogue book to speaking out loud; the line says only what the cover shows and the site says: finding the microphone and singing out loud. The link to vocabulary is loose (speaking up, not word learning), which Yarin may want to swap. Nothing about AI appears in the copy.

notes: Games research read on 2026-10-13 by a research subagent (the run was drawn 22:07 on 13 Oct). Stage language_vocabulary, ages 4 to 5. 3 suggestions tonight: 2 games and the LumeBook book. Both games are Kodkod (reviewer warning): the Israeli pool of games with a verified official age of 4 or lower and Israeli evidence was thin. Game 1 (מי אני ומה שמי?) is popular_in_israel on one strong signal: position 21 of 463 in Toys R Us Israel's best-selling sort (inside the top 10 percent, one place outside the top 20); game 2 (זיכרון קלאסי) rests on supporting signals only (position 167 of 463 plus several retailers plus Kodkod) and its vocabulary link is the weaker one, so the slide says a chance to name things aloud. Rankings are a store sales sort with an undisclosed window, not a published chart. Both packshots are Kodkod's own, 780 px, rights_unverified, so the carousel is not publish-ready until Yarin clears the images. Toys R Us spec fields were unreliable, so official ages come from Kodkod's pages and boxes. Not used: Stitch Ravensburger memory (no reliable official age), פנטומימה (6 to 8), Fox Mind games (mostly 5+).
